newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium up.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium up.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mixed on Monday, with gold futures weaker and palladium firmer following gains in the New York market on Friday, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen to 10 yen per gram lower, with benchmark April ending down three yen at 1,243 yen.

A report by the U.S. Federal Reserve late last week that the United States and other governments should sell a part of their gold reserves to boost their economies was seen as a bearish factor for gold.
"The report has cast a shadow over sentiment for gold," one trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $340.75/341.05 per ounce at 0732 GMT, against $340.80/341.30 in New York on Friday.

"Sentiment for gold remains bearish. In gold futures, private investors were slightly on the selling side, but the volume was low," the trader said, adding he pegged initial support for the spot gold price at around $337.0 per ounce.

Platinum futures were mixed. Weaker spot platinum prices dented nearby months of platinum futures, while the tight physical market and short-covering from private investors lifted all palladium futures, the traders said.

Although Russian platinum group metals agency Almaz said it would resume platinum group metal (PGM) exports soon, uncertainty over the amount it would sell supported the PGM market, especially palladium.
"There is talk Russian PGM exports to western countries this year will be much lower than last year," one trader said.
Platinum futures ranged from 46 yen per gram lower to 13 yen up. Benchmark April platinum was up seven yen at 1,368 yen.
Palladium ranged from two to 10 yen per gram up. Benchmark April palladium was up seven yen at 570 yen. Benchmark April silver was down 0.4 yen per 10 grams at 174.3 yen.
